curve/def: The sigmoid squashes any number into the range zero to one. Sigma of x is one over one plus e to the minus x.
curve/zero: At zero, e to the zero is one, so sigma is one over two: a half.
curve/two: At two, e to the minus two is about zero point one four. One over one point one four is about zero point eight eight.
curve/tails: Far to the right it creeps up toward one, and far to the left down toward zero. At minus two, it is zero point one two.
slope/rule: Its slope has a neat form: sigma times one minus sigma. Backprop can build it from the output it already has.
slope/two: At x equals two, that is zero point eight eight times zero point one two: about zero point one zero five.
slope/peak: The slope is steepest at zero: a half times a half, a quarter. It is never more than that.
slope/chain: In a graph, the sigmoid node multiplies the gradient from above by this local slope, so it shrinks the gradient at least four times.
flat/six: Far from zero the curve goes flat. At six, sigma is zero point nine nine seven five.
flat/tiny: So its slope is zero point nine nine seven five times zero point zero zero two five: about zero point zero zero two five.
flat/dead: Almost no gradient gets through. A saturated sigmoid, stuck near zero or one, passes almost nothing back to the nodes before it.
